faqs.question: How many friends do you need for a girl group costume?
faqs.answer: Three is the practical minimum, because two people read as a duo. Fixed casts like the March sisters or the Golden Girls need exactly four, while birthstones, the zodiac line-up and the decade timeline stretch from 3 to 12.

faqs.question: What are the cheapest girl group costume ideas?
faqs.answer: Undead bridesmaids and haunted spa night both come in at an estimated US$5–15 per person, because they reuse dresses, robes and towels the group already owns. The off-camera photographer role is the lowest-spend part of all, at an estimated under US$10.

faqs.question: Which group costumes need exactly four women?
faqs.answer: The March sisters from Little Women and the Golden Girls are both fixed at four, and Charlie's Angels is three, or four with a Bosley. If anyone might drop out, pick a set that flexes, such as phases of the moon or the timeline line-up.

faqs.question: What can a big group of 8 or more women dress up as?
faqs.answer: Phases of the moon fits eight exactly, and birthstones or the zodiac line-up go up to 12. A cappella rivals, pick 'n' mix and the weather forecast also work for 7 or more, at an estimated US$10–30 per person.

faqs.question: How do we pick a costume when our body types are all different?
faqs.answer: Choose a theme where the shared element is a colour, prop or role rather than a cut or size, and hand out parts by role. Becker and colleagues found occasional fat talk among 82–85% of women in every age group they surveyed, so set that ground rule before anyone tries anything on.

faqs.question: Are there modest girl group costumes for friends who cover up?
faqs.answer: Yes. The suffragettes, the March sisters, the Golden Girls and the Bletchley Park codebreakers are full-coverage as standard, and every set in the list works with long sleeves, full-length hems and a headscarf.

faqs.question: Do we need licensed outfits for a pop-culture squad?
faqs.answer: No. Colour, hair and one signature prop carry the reference, such as pink satin bombers for the Pink Ladies or silver wigs for the Golden Girls. Leave logos off anything you print, and never sell copies.

faqs.question: What if one friend in the group doesn't want to dress up?
faqs.answer: Give her the off-camera role as the paparazzo who takes the group shot, or an accessory-only part in a tiered theme. In the weather set, for example, fog is just a grey jumper.

faqs.question: Are these costumes suitable for teenage girls?
faqs.answer: Most are, especially the food, decade, cosy and nature sets. Skip the cocktail-dress glam looks for younger teens and agree a per-person budget cap before anyone shops.

faqs.question: Can I send one friend from the group her own Halloween card?
faqs.answer: Yes. SubhSandesh's interactive Halloween card has a best-friend mode that asks 'Will you be my boo-st friend forever?' and holds up to six photos. It is a one-person greeting page, so it does not invite or include the rest of the group.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Girl Group Halloween Costumes: 30 Ideas Sorted by Group Vibe

The best girl group Halloween costumes give each friend her own part in one readable theme, so 3 or 10 women can join without matching outfits. Here are 30 sets in 8 vibes, tagged with group size, estimated spend per person and a photo-ready score. The score matters because group shots travel by phone: SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone 48.3% of the time, and the average page draws 11.1 views, platform-wide rather than Halloween figures.

Halloween is fixed on 31 October, which is a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027. Plan the set about three weeks out.

## What makes a girl group costume work?

A girl group costume is a family of related looks worn by women friends, with each person playing one distinct piece of a shared idea. It succeeds when a stranger can name the theme from a single photo while every friend still picks her own silhouette, spend and coverage. Girls group costumes for teens follow the same logic.

Brackets give group size, est. per-person US$ for a wardrobe and charity-shop build plus one bought piece, and a 1–5 photo-ready score. That score is our call on how legible the theme is in one phone-sized group shot.

## 30 girl group Halloween costumes by group vibe

Vibes run from black tie to sofa. Mixed-budget groups should read section 8 first.

### 1. Glam and fashion groups (4 ideas)

These suit a dress code or club night. Most reuse something already hanging up.

- **Velvet vampire ball:** one jewel-tone velvet each, ruby through amethyst, with fangs. (3–6 · est. US$15–35 · 4/5)
- **Red-carpet nominees:** evening wear and a satin sash for an invented prize, "Best Haunting in a Supporting Role". (3 to 10+ · est. US$10–25 · 4/5)
- **Undead bridesmaids:** dresses from an old wedding party, grey face paint and wilted bouquets. (3–6 · est. US$5–15 · 5/5)
- **Widows' club:** black cocktail dresses, veiled fascinators, pearls and a scroll labelled "The Will". (3–4 · est. US$15–30 · 3/5)

### 2. Pop-culture squads (6 ideas)

Fictional girl gangs read instantly. Skip logos; colour, hair and one prop carry it.

- **The Pink Ladies:** pink satin bombers with first names ironed on, cigarette trousers, neck scarves. (3–6 · est. US$25–45 · 5/5)
- **The Plastics:** head-to-toe pink, one friend clutching a fake gossip notebook. (3–4 · est. US$10–25 · 4/5)
- **Charlie's Angels, 1970s TV:** feathered hair, flares, turtlenecks, posed back to back. (3, or 4 with a "Bosley" · est. US$15–30 · 4/5)
- **The March sisters:** Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy from *Little Women*, in shawls, with a fan, inkpot, sheet music and sketchbook. (exactly 4 · est. US$15–35 · 3/5)
- **The Golden Girls:** pastel blouses, roomy cardigans, silver wigs and a cheesecake. (exactly 4 · est. US$15–30 · 4/5)
- **A cappella rivals, Bellas-style:** identical blazers and neck scarves plus a pitch pipe. (7+ · est. US$15–30 · 4/5)

### 3. Nature and elements sets (4 ideas)

These scale with the guest list. Seasons and planets are everywhere already, so these go further.

- **Birthstones:** each friend wears her birth month's stone colour under a paper gem-cut crown. (up to 12 · est. US$10–20 · 3/5)
- **Phases of the moon:** eight phases in a row, new moon in black to full moon in silver. (8 ideal · est. US$10–25 · 4/5)
- **Zodiac line-up:** everyone plays her own star sign, say a crab-claw headband for Cancer. (up to 12 · est. US$10–20 · 3/5)
- **Weather forecast:** sun, rain cloud, thunderstorm, fog, snow, rainbow, plus a presenter with a pointer. (5–10 · est. US$10–25 · 4/5)

### 4. Food and dessert sets (4 ideas)

Colour does the work here. Choose pastel or rich, never both.

- **Box of macarons:** one pastel each, felt "shell" headbands, a cardboard lid as the sign. (5–6 · est. US$10–20 · 4/5)
- **Afternoon tea stand:** teapot, jam scone, cucumber sandwich, fruit tart, sugar bowl. (5–6 · est. US$15–30 · 3/5)
- **Box of chocolates:** brown, gold-foil and pink as truffle, praline and strawberry cream. (3–10 · est. US$10–25 · 3/5)
- **Pick 'n' mix:** cola bottle, jelly ring, foam banana and friends, with a paper scoop. (7+ · est. US$10–20 · 4/5)

### 5. "Everyone picks a decade" sets (3 ideas)

Each friend claims her own era, ending the fight over roles. Line up in date order.

- **Timeline line-up:** one decade apiece from the 1920s to the 2010s, each with a year card. (5–10 · est. US$10–30 · 4/5)
- **The little black dress, a century on:** all black, each cut from a different decade. (3–10 · est. US$10–30 · 3/5)
- **Dance crazes by decade:** Charleston, jitterbug, twist, hustle and voguing, each danced on cue. (5–6 · est. US$10–25 · 5/5)

### 6. Historical women sets (3 ideas)

These women worked in teams. Play the job and era, never a caricature, and never change anyone's skin tone.

- **Bletchley Park codebreakers:** 1940s skirt suits or navy uniforms and a "Top Secret" folder. By 1945, [75% of Bletchley Park's staff were women](https://www.bletchleypark.org.uk/our-story/who-were-the-codebreakers/), six in ten in uniform. (3–10 · est. US$15–35 · 3/5)
- **NASA's West Area Computers:** 1950s blouses, slacks and a slide rule. [Dorothy Vaughan ran NACA's segregated West Area Computing unit from 1949 to 1958](https://www.nasa.gov/people/dorothy-vaughan/); Mary Jackson and Katherine Johnson were among its alumni. (3–4 · est. US$15–30 · 3/5)
- **Suffragettes:** white blouses, long skirts and purple, white and green sashes, colours that [The National Archives says stood for freedom, purity and hope](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/education/teaching-resources/suffragettes-on-file-1840-1912/). (any · est. US$10–25 · 4/5)

### 7. Cosy and comfort groups (3 ideas)

Built for cold nights and floor-sitting house parties. Everything is wearable for six hours.

- **Haunted spa night:** bathrobes, hair towels and sheet face masks that turn into mummies when the lights dim. (any · est. US$5–15 · 4/5)
- **Book club of the dead:** long cardigans, pale make-up and a Gothic classic each, *Dracula* or *Carmilla*. (3–6 · est. US$5–20 · 3/5)
- **Hibernation den:** fleece hoodies with felt ears as hedgehog, dormouse, brown bear and bat, under one shared blanket. (3–6 · est. US$10–25 · 4/5)

### 8. Mixed sizes and budgets in one group (3 ideas)

These frameworks sit on top of any set above. They give the friend on a tight budget, or the costume sceptic, a real part.

- **Three-tier roles:** full, half and accessory-only parts; in the weather set, the rainbow is a US$40 build while fog is a grey jumper. (any · est. US$5–40 by tier · 4/5)
- **Shared palette, own silhouette:** fix two colours, emerald and black, and let each friend pick a dress, jumpsuit, abaya or jeans. (any · est. under US$15 · 3/5)
- **The off-camera role:** one friend comes as the paparazzo with a camera and shoots the group. (any · est. under US$10 · 3/5)

## Girl group costume vibes compared: size and est. cost per person

The eight vibes fold into five rows, one example each. Costs are per-person US$ estimates, not quotes.

| Group vibe | Example set | Group size | Est. cost per person |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glam and fashion | Undead bridesmaids | 3–6 | US$5–15 |
| Pop-culture squad | The Pink Ladies | 3–6 | US$25–45 |
| Nature, food and dessert | Phases of the moon | 7–8 | US$10–25 |
| Decade and history | Timeline line-up | 5–10 | US$10–30 |
| Cosy and mixed-budget | Haunted spa night | Any size | US$5–15 |

Owned-clothes sets come cheapest and bought matching jackets dearest. A friend on a smaller budget fits the first or last row best.

## How to theme a body-, budget- and modesty-diverse group

Body talk is a bigger risk than any costume. Surveying 914 women aged 18 to 87, [Becker and colleagues (*Journal of Eating Disorders*, 2013)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC3776206) found occasional "fat talk", the self-critical body chat friends trade, holding steady at 82–85% in all four age groups. They also cite earlier work where 3–5 minutes of it raised undergraduate women's body dissatisfaction.

So agree the rule before the fitting. The shared element should be a colour, prop or role, never a cut, hem or size.

Photos are the second pressure point. A [2016 *First Monday* study of 130 female college students](https://firstmonday.org/ojs/index.php/fm/article/view/6390) linked higher body dissatisfaction with taking more selfies, though not with posting more. It is correlation, not cause, but supports a three-take limit and one veto per friend.

- **Body-diverse:** hand out parts by role, not fit; capes, robes, sashes and headpieces suit most sizes.
- **Budget-diverse:** name a per-person cap, say US$20, before anyone shops, and let tiered roles absorb gaps.
- **Modesty-diverse:** every set works with long sleeves, full hems and a headscarf; the suffragettes, Golden Girls and March sisters need no changes.
- **Teen groups:** pick sets a parent would approve, such as cosy or decade ones.

## One friend from the squad: a bestie-mode Halloween card

The costume belongs to the group, but one friend may deserve something of her own. Our [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is built for a single recipient, not a crowd, and its best-friend mode ends on "Will you be my boo-st friend forever?".

Add both names, a letter and up to six costume photos. She knocks three times, carves a pumpkin, wipes fogged portraits to find your pictures and earns a Boo License sized for Instagram Stories, showing her photo and the costume you chose for her; you are emailed when she first answers.

For a voice message, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds up to 60 seconds of audio, 12 photos and a reply box. With 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators setting a password, lock yours too if other friends are in the photos.

## When a girl group costume, or the card, falls short

Fixed casts collapse when someone drops out: the March sisters and Golden Girls need exactly 4. Without a confirmed headcount by about 24 October, switch to birthstones or the timeline.

The card suits one recipient only, with an English-only interface and no group invitations, so a shared album serves ten friends better. If she is standing next to you on the night, hand her a printed group photo instead.

## Sources

- Becker, Diedrichs, Jankowski and Werchan, "I'm not just fat, I'm old", *Journal of Eating Disorders*, 21 February 2013.
- Wagner, Aguirre and Sumner, "The relationship between Instagram selfies and body image in young adult women", *First Monday*, 18 August 2016.
- Bletchley Park Trust, "Who were the Codebreakers?", undated.
- NASA, "Dorothy Vaughan", November 2016.
- The National Archives (UK), "Suffragettes on file", undated.

structuralLimitations: Brief asked for nature sets including seasons and planets; b1 group-halloween-costumes already uses four seasons, four elements and the solar system, so they are named only as 'already everywhere' and replaced by birthstones, moon phases, zodiac and weather.
Competitor pop-culture picks (Cheetah Girls, Heathers, Sailor Scouts, Barbies, Hocus Pocus) and sibling picks (Powerpuff Girls, Sanderson sisters, Spice Girls in 90s) were deliberately avoided.

Historical sets are groups (Bletchley Park, West Area Computers, suffragettes), none overlapping b3's Nellie Bly, Grace Hopper, Mary Shelley, Frida Kahlo, Mary Anning, Savitribai Phule, Bessie Coleman, Wilma Rudolph or Junko Tabei.
The National Archives glosses suffragette purple as 'freedom'; other accounts give 'dignity' or 'loyalty'. The post attributes the gloss to The National Archives rather than stating it as settled.
Becker 2013's 3–5 minute exposure finding is the paper's citation of Stice, Maxfield & Wells, reported as such, not Becker's own data.
Wagner 2016 is correlational, n=130 college women; the post says so.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page in the measured SERP that gives every set a group size, an estimated per-person cost and a photo score, and the only one that addresses body-, budget- and modesty-diverse groups with peer-reviewed sources; the top results are 2015–2024 listicles, one of them dead.
